analysis.title: Market Intelligence: US Morning Update
key_insights: Asia closed the week mixed. Hong Kong (+1.8%) and India outperformed, mainland China and Japan were flat, Taiwan and Korea were closed for a holiday.
European equities are trading higher (FTSE 100 +1.1%, DAX +1.3%, Euro STOXX 600 +1.1%) after a decline in regional sovereign yields and a pullback in oil prices.
US 10-year Treasury yield is a touch higher at 5.25% after a decline of about 10bps the prior day.

Credit focus: Amanda Lynam writes that a rise in rates volatility could reduce demand for both IG and HY credit and push spreads wider. If growth stays firm, credit can absorb higher rates. If sovereign risk or inflation drive rates higher, credit could be pressured.
Oil stays elevated even though Persian Gulf exports have recovered to 2025 levels. Yulia Grigsby attributes this to global visible stocks falling to near all-time lows.

GS models Brent spot as a long-run cost anchor plus a timespread, with the timespread split into inventory effects, interest-rate carrying costs and a residual risk premium. The updated model adds non-OECD visible oil stocks because OECD commercial stocks alone no longer explain the Brent 1M/36M timespread this year.
Brent carries a near-record geopolitical risk premium, which could keep prices above fair value longer if diplomatic tensions do not ease.

Energy: Mehta/Breno's fifth Ten Ideas report is built on four themes: oil E&P momentum (Buy COP, OXY, PR), power and LNG (Buy PWR, BKR, GLNG), refining (Buy DINO) and natural-gas upstream/midstream (TRP, AR).

Refining: GS stays constructive into 3Q26 earnings, sees upside to consensus estimates, and favors Buy-rated VLO, MPC and DINO. Focus areas are the mid-cycle margin outlook, light-heavy crude differentials and capital allocation.

Consumer: persistent inflation reduces spending flexibility for lower-income and lower-credit consumers, but overall consumer credit health remains constructive on low unemployment, modest leverage and stable aggregate delinquencies. GS economists forecast 2027 discretionary cash-flow acceleration across all income quintiles, with the lowest-income cohort lagging.
Consumer Buy list: FICO, DKS, ULTA, CHD, CL, EL, ELF, PEP, MNST, CELH, PM, MO, COF.
PepsiCo reported a slight Q3 beat but lowered FY26 EPS guidance, as GS expected, on continued North American pressure. GS maintains Buy.

Today's data: preliminary University of Michigan sentiment for October (GS 47.0, consensus 47.7, last 48.1) and 5-10-year inflation expectations (GS 3.4%, last 3.4%). Boston Fed President Collins speaks at 4:00 PM. DAL reports before the open.
Rating changes in Asia: Asahi Kasei (3407.T) cut to Neutral from Buy and Mitsui Chemicals (4183.T) cut to Sell from Neutral. No changes in the Americas or Europe.

Other notable research: HUM reclaims top-tier 4+ Stars status in GS's 2027 MA Stars analysis while ALHC lags peers. GS lowers its 3Q26 estimates for Venture Global but still sees upside risk to 2027. SpaceX's 800 MHz spectrum acquisition is flagged as a competition risk for US telcos.
